transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Li, Priya Patel, Marco Alvarez, Emily Chen, Alex Morgan, Samira Khan, Drew Patterson, Nina Ortiz, Kai Robinson

Summary:
Quick internal SE enablement focused on sharpening messaging, practicing a 12-minute demo script with explicit latency/cost talking points, and aligning on answers to security/compliance questions. Ran two role-play demos and collected objections to fold into the playbook.

00:00 Jordan Li: Okay team, thanks for being on time, we'll aim for 75 minutes, agenda first 20 for messaging, then two demo runs, then role play and action items.
00:18 Marco Alvarez: Quick housekeeping, please keep cameras on for demo feedback, and drop slide notes in the chat.
00:34 Priya Patel: I'll kick off with the one-liner and the 30-second elevator. Remember we want "developer-first inference with production economics" as the tag.
00:49 Alex Morgan: That phrasing works, but in the field people ask "how is that different from calling OpenAI?" —we need the crisp differentiator.
01:10 Priya Patel: Right. Suggested answer: Redwood emphasizes predictable latency and cost, routing and fallback policies, and private deployment options. So you can say: "We give the same simple API as hosted vendors, plus control over deployments, predictable reserved capacity, and tooling to lower per-token cost."
01:35 Samira Khan: Folks often jump straight to price, how much cheaper are we?
01:47 Jordan Li: Important to avoid hard numbers unless you have benchmarked workloads. Instead, lead with unit economics levers: batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization, and model routing. Then offer to run a quick benchmark.
02:05 Nina Ortiz: Also emphasize that Dedicated gives SLAs and isolation for regulated customers. Customers in finance ask about KMS/HSM and audit logs.
02:28 Priya Patel: Yes mention SOC 2 and optional on-prem. If they ask data residency, say we support region pinning and private deployments, but for very strict air-gapped needs we'll escalate to the Private team.
02:45 Drew Patterson: Quick question on tech: what's the simplest demo to highlight latency controls?
03:00 Priya Patel: Show a live chat prompt against a small context, then flip to a high-throughput batch of short completions to show the batching/cost tradeoff. Demonstrate a traced request in console so they see token cost and per-token latency.
03:25 Jordan Li: Ok demo run one — Priya you lead, I'll play the customer and throw objections. Try to hit these checkpoints: one-liner, architecture slide, live demo, fallback policy example, and pricing ask.
03:40 Priya Patel: Starting demo: "Hi, I'm using Redwood's API to power an in-app assistant..." (screen share) ... 04:15 (demo running) ... 05:02 Priya Patel: here we send a 120-token prompt and show streaming tokens. Notice the latency is about 220 ms per token on this model, and the console shows KV cache hits for earlier prefixes.
05:28 Jordan Li (as customer): That's nice, but what if we have strict PII concerns — will data leave our VPC?
05:40 Priya Patel: Good question. For Dedicated we offer private networking and an option to manage keys via your KMS. For on-prem or air-gapped, we have a Private deployment package; I'll follow up with the security brief.
06:05 Jordan Li: And what about model drift — how do we roll back when quality regresses?
06:18 Priya Patel: We version models in the catalog and support canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous variants. Also integrate evals and prompt-based regression alerts into Redwood Optimize.
06:40 Marco Alvarez: Note to the SEs: when talking about fallback, use a customer-story like "we had a marketplace use-case where traffic spiked and fallback kept the app online with a slightly cheaper variant". Concrete stories help.
07:05 Role play pause for feedback — Marco and Emily give notes on pace and clarity.
08:00 Second demo run. Alex to act as a skeptical engineering manager.
08:12 Alex Morgan: (as eng mgr) "We already self-host; why move to Redwood?"
08:20 Priya Patel: Lead with developer experience and ops savings. "Self-hosting means you own the ops and the optimizations; Redwood brings a runtime with smart routing, continuous batching, and a console for tracing and costing so you don't have to build those layers."
08:41 Alex Morgan: Engineers will ask about kernel optimization and quantization — what level of detail do we go into?
08:55 Priya Patel: High level: we select kernels and quantization profiles based on model and sequence-length distribution. For deep dives, say we'll schedule a technical deep-dive with the infra team.
09:20 Samira Khan: Competitor callouts — if someone mentions OpenAI, emphasize that OpenAI is great for quick experiments but lacks reserved capacity and private deployment options. For Anthropic, highlight differences in model catalog and ecosystem integrations.
10:05 Marco Alvarez: Watch the trap of saying "we're cheaper" — instead say "we give controls that can materially reduce per-token costs for production workloads" and offer examples.
10:30 Demo: show console tracing, cost per route, and a sample rollout policy. 11:15 show tracing graph and token breakdown.
11:40 Nina Ortiz: Someone asked about security certifications, do we have a concise line?
11:50 Emily Chen: "We are SOC 2 compliant, support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and integrate with customer KMS; for regulated deployments we offer Private on-prem options and audit logs."
12:12 Jordan Li: Time for the lightning objections list — we'll run rapid-fire answers. Priya you respond, others will pose.
12:22 Drew Patterson: "What about latency for long-context models?"
12:30 Priya Patel: A: "Long context increases per-token work; we mitigate with KV caching and model selection for long vs short sequences and optimize kernels for those access patterns."
12:44 Alex Morgan: "How do you price Dedicated?"
12:50 Jordan Li: A: "Reserved capacity pricing with monthly/annual commits — we typically pledge a baseline and measure burst capacity. We'll follow up with a benchmark-based quote."
13:10 Samira Khan: "What fallback looks like in a multi-region outage?"
13:18 Priya Patel: A: "Smart routing can failover to other regions or to a compatible cheaper variant; the console shows health and we can set SLO-based routing policies."
13:35 Marco Alvarez: Feedback: good to name the playbook page where the routing examples live.
13:50 Jordan Li: Wrap up — recap next steps and action items.
14:05 Emily Chen: I'll add the competitive bullets and quantization notes to the playbook and circulate tonight.
14:20 Jordan Li: Great. Thanks all. We'll run two dry-runs next week and collect top objections for next session.

End of meeting.
